parsed.explanation: The combined regime is dominated by national measures that reach every arrival. Passports show only M or F matching birth sex, and mismatched travellers face blocking, stranding, refusal and a possible permanent fraud bar. Federal immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men, and federal corrections has adopted a conversion-style policy with reported care denial. The state layer adds a minor-care ban, closure of its marker-change route, and a 2023 parental-notification requirement that can out minor visitors. Offsetting this, state law has no restroom restriction, its facility bill is not law, a 2019 hate-crime aggravator covers gender identity, and two cities protect restroom use. Enforcement data is absent, so street-level risk is not assessed. Rated as Elevated-to-High risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports issue only M or F matching birth sex since 2025; the Supreme Court allowed the restriction in Nov 2025. Mismatched travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and stranding. Cable instructs refusal on discrepancy and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending; no documented operative protection for visitors at entry.
entry_documents.interaction: The national entry regime governs all arrivals regardless of state. The state marker-change ban mainly affects residents, not visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-style policy from 2026 with hair cutting, hormone removal and reported care denial. Federal reporting of trans prisoner numbers stopped in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented beyond pending challenges to federal orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any detention under federal authority follows the national regime, whatever the state's own law. The state trespass-based bathroom offence does not apply in this jurisdiction.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent facility use in government-funded buildings. The facility bill passed the upper chamber 37-8 in Jan 2026 but is not law and had no lower-chamber hearing. Map notes other sex-defining laws may still affect access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state restroom restriction as of Apr 2026. Two cities protect restroom use by ordinance. A 2023 appellate injunction blocks school bathroom limits pending litigation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal building rules overlay the state's permissive stance. Enactment of the bill would add K-12 and university exclusion and prison housing by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: State bars gender-affirming surgery, puberty blockers and hormones for under-18s, and bars physicians from aiding it. Federal hospital subpoenas sought records for patients under 19. A proposed federal rule would bar reimbursement under 18.
care_services.protection: Availability of adult gender-affirming care is not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor visitor cannot obtain covered care here, and records of past care could be subpoenaed by federal authorities.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for rapid neutralisation. A cash-reward system targets leadership. A federal order directs prosecution of teachers who facilitate social transition. Official hostility is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target people who merely disagree. Several orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing mainly reaches advocates and schools. Its traveller-facing reach is indirect but real for visible advocates.

minors_guardians.exposure: State law requires written parental notification when a non-emancipated minor asks for a different name, pronoun or title. Minors cannot get transition care. Federal orders threaten prosecution of teachers and records subpoenas reach under-19 patients.
minors_guardians.protection: Appellate injunction against school bathroom restrictions is in place pending litigation.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's social transition can be disclosed to the accompanying guardian. The guardian may face inquiry where a school or clinic is involved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or police-directed targeting is documented for this state. Bias-crime enforcement data under the 2019 aggravator was not found. The 2025 criminal bathroom arrest occurred in a different jurisdiction and is excluded.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime aggravator covers gender identity. National hate-crime statute covers gender identity. Local ordinances protect some restroom use and employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Protection depends on locality. There is no statewide employment or public-accommodation protection for gender identity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Marker-change route closed 1 Feb 2026 and birth-certificate amendments barred. No statewide employment protection. City and county conversion-therapy bans are barred by state law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal employment ruling, national hate-crime statute, and pending federal and state suits. Some federal orders are enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies sit partly outside the state. Whether they operate at entry or in custody is unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.25-C has birth-sex housing, a criminal cross-dressing statute and arrests during family visits. This dossier has comparable custody harm through federal policy but no state housing mandate or criminal presentation statute. It sits above 0.25-C on visitor-facing criminal exposure and similar on custody harm.

Anchor 0.35-A has universal entry exclusion with no effective remedy and no imprisonment. This dossier has comparable refusal and stranding exposure, plus documented custody abuse and a possible lifetime bar. It is therefore slightly lower than 0.35-A, though its state layer is milder.

Anchor 0.55-B has secondary screening and administrative refusal without custody abuse. This dossier adds documented immigration-custody abuse and a possible permanent fraud ineligibility, so it sits materially below 0.55-B.

Anchor 0.75-D has a statute protecting gender identity, a police review board that operates, and prosecution of attackers. This dossier has a hate-crime aggravator and local protections, but no statewide protection, no operating remedy for documents and no custody protection. Reaching 0.75 would require protected entry, custody safeguards, and a working statewide anti-discrimination regime.

parsed.synthesis: The national entry regime and federal custody practices are the operative exposures for a visitor with mismatched documents. These include passport blocking, refusal with a possible lifetime bar, and documented abuse in immigration custody. The state adds a minor-care ban, a parental-notification duty that can out a travelling child, and a closed marker-change route. The state's absence of a restroom ban and its hate-crime aggravator soften the state layer somewhat. Visitors with consistent documents face lower everyday exposure than those whose documents mismatch. Remedies are pending and unproven. Violence and enforcement data are undocumented, so the rating does not treat that absence as safety.
